applies_why: This text rules on a collision involving Matthew 1:16 and the parties' chain answers, so it is the kind of link adjudication K-C governs.
quote: D1 vs C2 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings; the defender answered the beget-pattern and naming witnesses in [CR3] LINK 4 and [CR2] §5, and the challenger answered hēs in [DR3] C2.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: "never verse by verse" — either the rule forbids deciding the link from whether Matthew 1:16 alone is underdetermined, or it permits noting individual verse ambiguity as part of a chain-by-footing decision; the judge used the isolated verse's ambiguity as the determination.
why: The judge labels Matthew 1:16 underdetermined from its own passive/feminine grammar admitting two readings, which is a verse-by-verse determination rather than a chain-against-chain weighing by footing under K-C.
